newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - policy set to meet inflation target.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - policy set to meet inflation target.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday policy will be set to meet the government's 2.5 percent target for underlying inflation.
"Policy is set to meet our inflation target. That is why we are sustaining our best inflation record in 50 years," Clarke said in a statement.
Underlying retail price inflation jumped to 3.3 percent year-on-year in October from 2.9, figures just released showed.
Headline inflation jumped to 2.7 percent year-on-year, from 2.1, although both figures were unchanged on the month.

Clarke noteed that retail prices were actually unchanged between September and October. "The reason the annual inflation rate is higher is because this time last year there was the largest fall in retail prices in any October since the war," he said.
